newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firmer, Brent hovers at $18.40.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firmer, Brent hovers at $18.40.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed $1.00 firmer on Wednesday, having held on to early gains made in the wake of a late Brent rally on Tuesday.
Brent was virtually unchanged from last night's close with strong bearish sentiment about the resumption of Iraqi exports balanced by prompt tightness in the U.S. gasoline market.

August gas oil closed at $163.75 a tonne, while August Brent, which expires at the close of business, was trading one cent up at $18.40 a barrel at 1658 GMT. The front spread was trading just in backwardation with September Brent at $18.37.
Strength at the front end of the market helped to push the front Brent spread out of contango, brokers said.
Data from the U.S. Department of Energy indicated a 3.9 million barrels draw on gasoline stocks last week.
"The market sentiment is for crude to go lower, but prompt gasoline in the States is pretty tight and at the front end gasoline cracks have widened out a lot recently," said one dealer.
Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal could reach 1.5 million barrels per day in August, with virtually all of this quarter's $1-billion of sales concentrated in that month.

Western diplomats at the United Nations said on Tuesday that Iraq would be allowed to carry over only five percent of its sales in the current 90 day sales period, which started on June 8, to the next quarter.
This would mean Iraq, having delayed the restart of exports for two months, will have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than previously expected, or forego some of its sales.
"At the moment the North Sea crude looks fairly stable but there is a feeling that with Iraq pumping quite a bit and come September the market will be well-supplied," said one.
Exports in the first six-month term of the scheme averaged around 660,000 bpd.
